activities.title: Count the calendar months and hours
activities.intro: Work it out from the rule, then type your answer.

items.q: Your applicant will apply in June (month 6). What is the earliest month number in which the training you certify under 61.39(a)(6)(i) may have been logged?
items.why: Within 2 calendar months preceding the month of application: April (4) and May (5) [[60:219|14 CFR 61.39(a)(6)]].

items.q: A pilot completed a flight review in March 2026 and nothing else that substitutes for one. Through which month of 2028 (month number) may he act as PIC?
items.why: He needs a review since the beginning of the 24th calendar month before the month of the flight. For a March 2028 flight that month is March 2026; for April 2028 it is April 2026, so March is the last month [[60:237|14 CFR 61.56(c)]].

items.q: A pilot logged six approaches, holding and course tracking in January (month 1) and nothing since. What is the last month number in which that experience lets her act as PIC under IFR?
items.why: The tasks must be within the 6 calendar months preceding the month of the flight. For July those months are January to June; for August, January drops out [[60:239|14 CFR 61.57(c)(1)]].

items.q: How many hours of instrument flight training in an airplane must an instrument-airplane applicant receive within 2 calendar months before the practical test?
items.why: Three hours from an authorized instructor in an appropriate airplane [[60:251|14 CFR 61.65(d)(2)(i)]].

items.q: Of an instrument-airplane applicant's 40 hours of instrument time, how many must come from an authorized instructor who holds an instrument-airplane rating?
For how many years must you keep the record of each person you endorsed for a practical test?

activities.title: Run a flight review the AC 61-98E way
activities.intro: Put the steps in order, first to last, then tap Check.
steps: Interview the pilot and review the logbook for time and recency
Agree on how the review will run and what counts as satisfactory
Write a plan of action: subjects, maneuvers, sequence and location
Review part 91 rules and operational knowledge on the ground
Fly the maneuvers inside a realistic scenario
Debrief with a comprehensive analysis of the performance
Endorse with A.69, or log dual instruction given
activities.why: Sequence from AC 61-98E: pre-review interview and logbook [[15:23|AC 61-98E 4.2]] [[15:25|AC 61-98E 4.2.3]], agreement [[15:25|AC 61-98E 4.2.4]], plan of action [[15:25|AC 61-98E 4.3]], part 91 and oral review [[15:26|AC 61-98E 4.3.1]] [[15:27|AC 61-98E 4.3.5.3]], maneuvers in a realistic scenario [[15:28|AC 61-98E 4.3.5.5]], debrief [[15:28|AC 61-98E 4.4]], and the endorsement or dual entry [[15:28|AC 61-98E 4.4.1]] [[15:29|AC 61-98E 4.4.2]].

activities.title: An IPC, one decision at a time
activities.intro: Maria owns a glass-panel C172 you know well. She is instrument rated but last flew approaches two years ago. You are a CFII with instrument ratings on both certificates. Make each call.

steps.s: Maria asks whether six approaches with a safety pilot will make her current again.
options: Yes, any six approaches will do it
No, after this long only an IPC will
Yes, if she flies them in an ATD
No, she must retake the practical test
steps.why: She has failed to meet 61.57(c) for more than six calendar months, so only an IPC reestablishes currency [[60:240|14 CFR 61.57(d)(1)]]. No new practical test is required.

steps.s: How do you shape the check before the flight?
options: Use one fixed IPC profile for everyone
Let her choose the tasks she likes
Skip planning; the ACS table is enough
Discuss her flying, then plan realistic scenarios
steps.why: Tailor the IPC to the pilot as with a flight review [[15:30|AC 61-98E 5.1.3]] and use a plan of action with realistic scenarios [[15:31|AC 61-98E 5.1.3.3]].

steps.s: She asks to do the whole IPC in the school's basic ATD (BATD) to save money.
options: Fine, any approved ATD may be used
Fine, as long as you sit beside her
Not allowed: only an AATD may be used
Only the holding task may be done there
steps.why: Only advanced ATDs may be used for the IPC, and the letter of authorization sets the credit [[15:30|AC 61-98E 5.1.2]].

steps.s: In the airplane, she is under the hood in busy VFR airspace. Who scans for traffic?
options: You do, throughout the flight
She does; it is her check
Nobody; ATC handles it on IFR
The traffic display handles it
steps.why: With a view-limiting device it is the flight instructor's responsibility to stay vigilant for other aircraft throughout the flight [[15:31|AC 61-98E 5.1.3.1]].

steps.s: Her approaches are good, but partial-panel attitude flying is not satisfactory even after some instruction.
options: Endorse it; approaches are what matter
Write 'IPC failed' in her logbook
Log dual given, debrief and plan training
Endorse it with a full-panel limitation
steps.why: The pilot must show satisfactory basic attitude instrument flying [[15:32|AC 61-98E 5.3]]. Do not endorse an unsatisfactory IPC; log dual instruction given [[15:33|AC 61-98E 5.4.1]] and no unsatisfactory entry is required [[12:53|AC 61-65K A.71]].

steps.s: Two lessons later she flies the whole IPC to standard. What do you write?
options: The A.69 flight review endorsement
The A.71 IPC endorsement, with make and model
The A.44 practical test endorsement
Nothing; currency comes back on its own
steps.why: A.71 certifies completion of the IPC of 61.57(d) in a named make and model on a date [[12:53|AC 61-65K A.71]], with your full signature block [[12:40|AC 61-65K A-7]].

activities.title: True or false: the professional instructor
activities.intro: Decide if each statement is true or false.

cards.s: Sincerity means being straightforward and honest with the learner at all times.
Criticizing a slow learner is fine as long as you do it in private.
cards.why: False. The AIH compares it to a doctor reprimanding a patient for not getting well fast enough; acceptance and support encourage learning [[25:167|AIH 8-9]].

cards.s: The AIH calls common courtesy perhaps the most important personal habit.
Reacting differently to the same error on different days is acceptable if your mood explains it.
cards.why: False. The successful instructor avoids it and keeps a calm, disciplined demeanor [[25:167|AIH 8-9]].

cards.s: Successful instructors can relax about their qualifications once certificated.
cards.why: False. They do not become complacent and keep looking for ways to improve [[25:168|AIH 8-10]].

cards.s: Continued use of outmoded procedures usually involves rationalization.

activities.title: Seven ways to cut frustration, in the instrument airplane
activities.intro: Drag each instrument training example to the method in Figure 8-4 it shows.

pins.label: Tie the hold lesson to the busy airports he flies into
Show the syllabus and the stage check date
Plan around each learner's background, not the class average
'Your level-off at the MDA was right on'
Explain why she chased the glideslope and how to fix it
The same approach standard every lesson
'I gave you the wrong frequency. My mistake.'

activities.why: The seven methods of AIH Figure 8-4 and the text beside it [[25:162|AIH 8-4]].
